results.question: Summarize the three laboratory experiments covered by this report.
results.answer:
The report covers three experiments conducted during the spring semester, all assembled on solderless breadboards and verified with a mixed-signal oscilloscope [Blocks 1-12]:

- **Lab 04 – 4-to-1 multiplexer:** Implemented with the 74HC153 integrated circuit, its function is to select one of four data inputs and route it to a single output under the control of select lines S1 and S0. The truth table was verified for all sixteen select-and-data combinations, and propagation delay measured 14 nanoseconds typical [Blocks 1-12].
- **Lab 05 – Inverting operational amplifier:** Built around a TL072 op-amp with a 10 kilo-ohm input resistor and 100 kilo-ohm feedback resistor. The measured voltage gain was -9.8, within 2 percent of the ideal -10, and the measured bandwidth at the -3 decibel point was 48 kilohertz [Blocks 1-12].
- **Lab 06 – 4-bit synchronous counter:** Used the 74LS163 integrated circuit clocked at 1 kilohertz. The counter advanced through all sixteen states from 0000 to 1111 without skipped or stuck states, and the ripple carry output enabled correct cascading; a clear input fault was observed when the clear line was asserted for fewer than 20 nanoseconds [Blocks 1-12].

All three circuits met their design targets, with limitations noted regarding breadboard contact resistance and room-temperature-only counter testing [Blocks 13-15].
